questions.question: Define a sole trader, capital, assets, liabilities, owner's equity and drawings, giving an example of each from a car wash business.
questions.expected_answer: Sole trader: a business owned by one person who supplies capital, takes all profit and bears all risk with unlimited liability (the car wash owner). Capital: money or assets the owner contributes (R50 000 savings deposited). Assets: possessions of the business that bring future benefits — non-current (high-pressure washer, vacuum cleaners) and current (bank, cash float, debtors). Liabilities: debts owed to outsiders — non-current (bank loan over four years) and current (creditors such as the soap supplier). Owner's equity: the owner's interest = capital + profit − drawings. Drawings: money or goods taken by the owner for private use (R6 000 for groceries).

questions.question: A car wash earned R48 000. Wages were R18 000, water and electricity R4 500 and cleaning materials R3 500. Capital was R50 000 and drawings R6 000. Calculate profit and owner's equity, and explain why drawings are not an expense.
questions.expected_answer: Total expenses = 18 000 + 4 500 + 3 500 = R26 000. Profit = 48 000 − 26 000 = R22 000. Owner's equity = 50 000 + 22 000 − 6 000 = R66 000. Drawings are not an expense because they are not incurred to earn income; they are a private withdrawal by the owner and reduce owner's equity directly, not profit.

questions.question: Explain debit and credit and the DEAD rule. State on which side each of the following increases: bank, capital, loan, current income, wages, drawings.
questions.expected_answer: Debit is the left side and credit the right side of an account; every transaction has equal debits and credits. Accounts on the left of A = OE + L (assets) increase on the debit side; accounts on the right (owner's equity, liabilities) increase on the credit side. Income increases OE so increases on the credit side; expenses and drawings decrease OE so increase on the debit side. DEAD: debits increase expenses, assets and drawings. Bank: debit. Capital: credit. Loan: credit. Current income: credit. Wages: debit. Drawings: debit.
